purpose: Re-run of the README's worked example on the current pipeline. The example shown in README.md had been captured on 0.1.0, an architecture that pruned to a shortlist and no longer exists, so the caption had to disclaim the demo directly beneath it.
prompt: /creative-problem-solving:ideas We keep losing senior engineers to bigger companies at around the 18-month mark. Comp is already competitive — we benchmark and we match. It's not the money. What can we actually do about this? This is all the information available, so don't ask me any questions; where something is missing, make a reasonable assumption and state it in your response.
rubric: Tests the ruled-out constraint rather than obeying it — probes whether 'it's not the money' actually holds before setting money aside
At least one option questions the framing — whether losing senior engineers at 18 months is necessarily the problem to solve
why_this_matters: The 0.1.0 run took 'it's not the money' at face value while the plain baseline refused the premise and was right to. That loss produced Phase 0's premise-testing step. This is the first run in which that step is measured on the problem that caused it, and an independent judge scored the claim as passing.
caveat: ONE REP. evals/README.md is explicit that the signal is a claim's pass rate across three or more reps. This shows the premise test fired on this run, not that it reliably fires.
